newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Friday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 24,000 yuan ($2,892) per tonne, rising 20 yuan. It opened at 24,200 and hit a high of 24,300 yuan.
April was unchanged at 23,570, May fell 50 to 23,650, June rose 20 to 24,000, August 100 to 24,000 and September 250 to 24,000.
Combined volume rose to 44,220 tonnes from 34,710.
Copper opened higher on LME gains but fell steadily on profit-taking for most of the session as market trend remained unclear, traders said.
"Investors were not very interested in staying in the market given the lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
Traders said copper was likely to move around the key 24,000 yuan level early next week.

Aluminium ended mixed in slow trading. The April contract fell 30 yuan to 16,320 yuan ($1,966) per tonne, May was unchanged at 16,680 and June rose 30 to 16,960. Combined volume fell to 1,690 tonnes from 1,820. ($1=8.2960 yuan)
